Concept illustration · Not a product screenshot
01

The problem

Everyday work crosses apps: drafting an email, proposing a meeting, or making sense of a browser page. Forma explores a voice-first way to connect those tasks while keeping the user in control.

02

The implementation

The prototype connects a React interface to FastAPI and a LangGraph workflow. Ollama handles local inference, whisper.cpp transcribes audio, and Playwright supports restricted browser-page reading.

03

An engineering decision

Permission is part of the workflow. Browser-read approvals are tied to a session, URL, expiration, and a single-use interrupt identifier. Clarification and cancellation are explicit states, rather than assumptions hidden inside a prompt.

04

What it demonstrates

The documented implementation supports voice and text input, email drafts, meeting proposals, and page summaries. Per-session locking and temporary audio processing help keep concurrent interactions isolated.

05

Context & limitations

Hackathon prototype. This is a description of the documented implementation, not a claim of production deployment or broad task reliability.
